phase2.errorMessage:
Done

(No error — but the program won't exit! The thread pool keeps the JVM alive.)
phase2.explanation:
No error printed, no crash — [[warn:but the program just hangs, and never actually exits]].

[[key:an ExecutorService's thread pool keeps running (and keeps the JVM alive) until it's explicitly told to stop]] — creating the pool doesn't come with any automatic cleanup, unlike a daemon thread from a couple lessons back which the JVM was happy to abandon on exit.

The fix is calling shutdown() once there's no more work to submit:

ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2);
pool.execute(() -> System.out.println("Done"));
pool.shutdown();  // lets queued/running tasks finish, then lets the JVM exit

shutdown() alone is usually enough — it doesn't block, it just stops accepting new work and lets the JVM exit once existing tasks finish. Add awaitTermination(timeout, unit) right after it if the rest of the program genuinely needs to wait for those tasks to finish before moving on.

mcq.question:
You need to run 5 independent tasks and each one needs to return a computed result that the main thread will use afterward. Which is the right combination?

A) pool.execute() for each task, since execute() is simpler
B) pool.submit() for each task, then call .get() on each returned Future
C) new Thread() for each task, storing results in a shared static field
D) pool.shutdown() called before submitting any tasks

phase4.selfChallenge:
Write a program that:
1. Creates a FixedThreadPool with 4 threads
2. Submits 10 tasks that print "Task X on thread Y" with X being 1-10
3. Uses Future to submit tasks and get results
4. Shuts down the pool properly

Bonus: Use submit() with Callable that returns the task number.

phase5.trivia: The Executor Framework was introduced in Java 5 (2004) by Doug Lea, the same engineer largely responsible for java.util.concurrent as a whole — before that, every thread pool in Java had to be hand-rolled from raw Thread and synchronized primitives.
